newsitem.title: USA: CME live cattle seen lower, feeder cattle steady.
newsitem.headline: CME live cattle seen lower, feeder cattle steady.

text.p: CME live cattle futures were expected to open 0.100 to 0.200 cent lower while feeder cattle were called steady, analysts said.

A decline in fed cattle prices late Tuesday, recent slow boxed beef movement and weak technicals are seen pressuring live cattle futures. After the futures close Tuesday, fed cattle traded $1 per cwt lower at $63 in the Texas-Oklahoma panhandle and Kansas feedlot areas and adequate nearterm cattle supplies should keep markets pressured, analysts said.
But support could develop as futures are near the low end of the recent trading range, they said.

Feeder futures were seen trading around the previous level on mixed market factors. A higher CME feeder cattle index could offset expected pressure from steady to higher corn futures indications, they said.

However, there was some concern that feeder cattle marketings would be rising soon. There was talk in the pit Tuesday that 20,000 head of feeders will on auction at Oklahoma City on Monday, they added.
The latest CME feeder cattle index was up $0.27 at $70.32 per cwt.
